name: manual_f6cbb9
claim: Choose the canonical representation before choosing a hash. Exact-byte hashing is correct for Git blobs, tracked files, and binary transport, where an exact byte identity is the actual invariant. It is wrong when applied to a mutable external text field (e.g. a GitHub PR/issue body) whose transport (JSON serialization, CLI output, shell command substitution) does not preserve incidental bytes such as a trailing newline -- comparing raw bytes there creates false-positive integrity failures on genuinely correct writes, not stronger integrity

decisions.notes: 2026-09-13 incident, oramasys/orama-system PR #357: a post-write integrity guard (added to close a real concurrent-edit race in scripts/cursor/append-pr-body.sh) compared raw SHA-256 hashes of a locally-written file (printf '%s\n', which adds a trailing newline) against the same content re-read through the GitHub API. The two never matched, even on a correct write, because command substitution and JSON text fields do not preserve that added byte -- confirmed with a direct, minimal reproduction (12 bytes vs 11) before fixing by normalizing (rstrip newline) before hashing. Two full domains exist and must not be conflated: Git blob / tracked artifact / binary payload -> exact bytes; GitHub PR/issue text metadata -> canonical logical text representation with transport newline semantics explicitly defined. Full write-up: .agent/memory/working/ORAMA_PR357_PR_BODY_INTEGRITY_FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_RECOVERY_2026-09-13.md.
